A step-by-step tutorial for analyzing flow cytometry data in R, built around the Cytek Aurora spectral flow cytometer. The pipeline covers everything from loading FCS files through statistical analysis.

The example data used throughout is the GvHD dataset from the `flowCore` package — a longitudinal study of bone marrow transplant patients. It runs on conventional flow cytometry data, so a few steps differ from Aurora data (notably the transformation step). Differences are clearly noted in each script.

---

## Why R and not FlowJo?

FlowJo is the standard in most flow labs and it's good at what it does — fast, visual, and familiar. But it has a reproducibility problem. When you gate in FlowJo, the decisions you make live in a workspace file that isn't human-readable and doesn't travel well. You can't easily version-control it, diff it, or hand it to a collaborator who has a different FlowJo version.

In R, every decision is written down. The gate boundaries are in the code. The transformation parameters are in the code. The statistical model is in the code. If a reviewer asks why you used arcsinh with a cofactor of 150, you can point to the line. If you need to rerun the analysis six months later with one sample excluded, you change one line and rerender.

The other practical advantage is that R keeps the entire analysis — from raw FCS files to final statistics — in one place. FlowJo exports numbers to Excel, Excel feeds GraphPad Prism, Prism generates figures. Every handoff is a place where something can go wrong. R eliminates those handoffs.

FlowJo still has a real role for exploratory gating during panel development or quick QC checks. This pipeline is for the analysis you'd actually report.

## Tutorial scripts

| Script | What it covers |
|--------|----------------|
| [01: Load and Metadata](scripts/01_load_and_metadata.html) | FCS format, flowFrame/flowSet, the three stages of flow data, loading and attaching metadata |
| [02: QC](scripts/02_qc.html) | Temporal instability, margin events, PeacoQC |
| [03: Transformation](scripts/03_transformation.html) | Checking `$PnE`, arcsinh vs. pre-transformed data |

## Setup

Install the required packages. The example data (`GvHD`) is built into the `flowCore` package and loads with a single line in script 01 — no files to download.

```r
# CRAN
install.packages(c("tidyverse", "uwot", "lme4", "emmeans", "gridExtra"))

# Bioconductor
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install(c("flowCore", "flowWorkspace", "openCyto", "ggcyto", "PeacoQC", "FlowSOM"))
```

Then work through the scripts in order, starting with [01: Load and Metadata](scripts/01_load_and_metadata.html). Script 01 will walk you through setting up a working directory before any files are saved.
